definition_zh: 正式地；官方地；据官方说法；以公职身份
definition_en: in a way that comes from or is approved by an authority, in one's formal public role, according to the public record, or by due formal procedure
core_image: 一枚刻着徽记的印章落在文件末页，红色的印痕慢慢干透
scene: 清晨的会议室里，长桌两端坐满人，秘书把盖好章的公告放进文件夹，等时间一到就发出去。The new rules were officially announced on Monday morning.
sceneCN: 这里的 officially 是「正式地、由官方宣布」（第 1 个义项：经权威渠道公布）；句意为新规定在星期一上午正式宣布。图中可辨识物件：长桌、公告、印章。

pos.zh: 正式地；官方地；以公职身份

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 officium（职务、义务）经法语进入英语，义为「官方的；正式的」
由 official 加 -dom 构成，义为「官僚；官场」
由 official 与 -ese 构成，指公文里常见的「官样腔调」

senses.title: Announced or approved by an authority
senses.definition: in a way that is stated, approved or confirmed by a person or body holding authority
senses.definitionCN: 由掌握权威的人或机构宣布、批准或确认的方式
senses.example: The results were officially announced on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 结果在星期五正式公布。
senses.why: The Latin noun officium named a duty attached to a post, so what is officially said is what someone with a post has the right to declare.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 officium 指附在职位上的职责，因此 officially 说出的，就是有职位的人有权宣布的内容，词的重点落在「谁有权说」。

senses.title: In one's public role or capacity
senses.definition: as part of one's public duties rather than as a private person
senses.definitionCN: 作为公职职责的一部分，而不是以私人身份行事
senses.example: She was there officially, representing the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她是以公职身份到场的，代表的是那个部门。
senses.why: Because officium also named the service owed to a position, the adverb marks the capacity in which a person acts rather than the private person.
senses.whyCN: officium 也指一个职位所应尽的差事，所以这个副词标的是一个人以何种身份行事，而不是他作为私人是谁。

senses.title: According to the public record, though perhaps not in fact
senses.definition: as reported or recorded in public by officials, often with a hint that the reality may differ
senses.definitionCN: 按官员对外公布或记录的说法，常暗示真实情况可能不同
senses.example: Officially the road is open, but the barrier is still down.
senses.exampleCN: 官方说这条路已经开放，可栏杆还放下来着。
senses.why: A claim that carries the stamp of an office is only the version on record, and speakers use officially to set that version against what they can see for themselves.
senses.whyCN: 带官印的说法只是记录在案的那一版，于是人们用 officially 把这一版和自己亲眼所见对起来，话里常藏着怀疑。

senses.title: By due formal procedure
senses.definition: in a formal or legal way, following the steps required for a change to count
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或合法的方式，走完让一项变动生效所需的手续
senses.example: He officially resigned at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 他在月底正式辞职。
senses.why: If a post is what makes an act official, then an act becomes final only when the proper steps are closed, and the adverb names that closing step.
senses.whyCN: 既然职位使一个举动成为官方举动，那么这个举动只有在手续走完时才算落定，副词指的正是这最后一步。

intro.en: Officially is the adverb of official, and official reached English from Latin officium by way of French; the whole family keeps the idea of a duty tied to a post.
intro.cn: officially 是 official 的副词，而 official 由拉丁语 officium 经法语进入英语；这一族词始终围绕「附在职位上的职责」这个意思。

items.en: Officium meant a duty, a service or the work attached to a public post, and it joined ops, wealth or power, with the verb facere, to do.
items.cn: officium 指职责、服务或附在公职上的事务，一般认为是 ops（财力、权力）与动词 facere（做）结合而成。

items.en: Officialis described what belonged to a magistrate or to a duty, and it passed into French as a word for an office holder and for what such a person does.
items.cn: officialis 形容属于长官或职务的事物，进入法语后既指任职者，也指这类人所办的事。

items.en: Old French officiel carried the sense of what is publicly authorized, and English borrowed it with that stamp of authority intact.
items.cn: 古法语 officiel 带着「经公开授权」的意思，英语借入时把这层权威印记一并保留。

items.en: Middle English used official for church officers and for things said by authority, and -ly later turned it into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 中古英语用 official 指教会官员和由权威说出的事，后来 -ly 把它变成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English adds officially to announcements, to the capacity in which someone acts, to public claims that may be doubted, and to steps that make a change final.
items.cn: 现代英语把 officially 用在公告、行事身份、可能存疑的公开说法，以及让变动生效的程序步骤上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for duty and office; the near-meaning group collects adverbs for public, formal and recorded statement.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在表示「职责、职务」的拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示公开、正式、记录在案的说法副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is official wearing -ly, and official is a Latin duty-noun turned adjective, so every hook returns to a post and the rights that come with it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 official 穿上 -ly，而 official 是拉丁语「职责」名词变来的形容词，所以每条记忆钩子都回到职位以及随之而来的权力。

normal.en: Official plus -ly gives officially, the ordinary way English builds a manner adverb from an adjective.
normal.cn: official 加 -ly 得到 officially，这是英语由形容词构成方式副词的常规做法。

normal.en: Officium joined a word for wealth or power with facere, to do, so the core picture is work done because a post requires it.
normal.cn: officium 把表示财力或权力的词与 facere（做）结合起来，核心画面是因职位要求而做的事。

normal.en: Official is also a noun for a person who holds a post, which is why officially can mean 'in that person's capacity'.
normal.cn: official 也可作名词指担任职务的人，所以 officially 能表示「以那个人的身份」。

normal.en: Officially announced and officially opened are fixed pairings: the adverb tells us the source of the approval.
normal.cn: officially announced 与 officially opened 是固定搭配：副词点明批准来自哪里。

normal.en: When a sentence begins with officially, expect a 'but' later; the word often sets the record against the reality.
normal.cn: 句子以 officially 开头时，后面多半有一个「可是」；这个词常把记录与现实并排摆出。

abstract.en: A word built on duty quietly asks who has the right to speak, not just whether the statement is true.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「职责」上的词，悄悄追问的是谁有权说话，而不只是话是否属实。

abstract.en: The same adverb can mean both 'authorized' and 'merely on paper', which is how official language earns its reputation.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词既能表示「已获授权」，也能表示「只是纸面上」，官方话语的名声正由此而来。

abstract.en: To do something officially is to let a procedure finish the act, as if the last signature did the real work.
abstract.cn: 正式地做一件事，就是让程序来完成这个举动，仿佛真正干活的是最后那个签名。

examples.en: The bridge was officially opened by the mayor.
examples.cn: 这座桥由市长正式启用。

examples.en: Officially she is on holiday, though her phone never stops.
examples.cn: 官方说法是她在休假，可她的电话一直响个不停。

examples.en: The company officially became a charity last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天正式成为慈善机构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费事里」——盖章办事得跑一趟，费事里透着正式；记住 officially 是正式地。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a duty tied to a post; from it come the authorized announcement, the capacity in which one acts, the record that may be doubted, and the procedure that makes a change final.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是附在职位上的职责；由此分出经授权的宣布、行事的身份、可能存疑的记录，以及让变动生效的程序。

definition_zh: 哦；哎呀（表示惊讶、领会、迟疑或招呼）
definition_en: an interjection used to show surprise, to acknowledge that one understands, to hesitate while thinking, or to call someone's attention
core_image: 一个人听到意外消息，嘴巴微张，一声短促的气从喉咙里出来
scene: 深夜的实验室只亮着一盏台灯，学生盯着刚打印出来的曲线，数据和预想的完全相反。Oh, that cannot be right.
sceneCN: 这里的 oh 表示惊讶（第 1 个义项：吃惊、意外）；句意为「哦，这不可能对吧」，说话人不敢相信眼前的结果。图中可辨识物件：台灯、打印纸、曲线。

pos.zh: 感叹词：表示惊讶、领会、迟疑或招呼

derivatives.zh: 由 oh 拉长元音并加写一个字母而来，语气更夸张，义为「哟；哎呀」
由 oh 重复并以连字符连接而成，用来表示「糟了、要出事」
由 oh 与 so 用连字符复合而成，口语里表示「极其、非常」，常带调侃

senses.title: Surprise or sudden emotion
senses.definition: used to express surprise, shock or a sudden strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用来表达惊讶、震动或突然涌起的强烈情绪
senses.example: Oh, I did not expect to see you here.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，我没想到会在这儿见到你。
senses.why: A short open vowel burst is the body's first reaction to something unexpected, and English fixed that sound as the word oh.
senses.whyCN: 短促张开的一声元音，是身体遇到意外时最直接的反应，英语就把这个声音固定成了 oh。

senses.title: Acknowledging that one understands
senses.definition: used as a short reply to show that the speaker has heard and understood
senses.definitionCN: 用作简短应答，表示说话人听到了并且明白了
senses.example: Oh, I see what you mean now.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，我现在明白你的意思了。
senses.why: Once the same sound answers another person, it stops being pure feeling and becomes a signal that the message has landed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个声音一旦用来回应别人，就不再只是纯粹的情绪，而成了「话已经接收到」的信号。

senses.title: Hesitating while thinking
senses.definition: used, often lengthened, to hold the floor while the speaker searches for words
senses.definitionCN: 常用拖长的形式，在说话人找词时占住发言的位置
senses.example: Oh, let me think for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，让我想一会儿。
senses.why: Drawing the sound out fills the silence, so oh turns into a small tool for keeping one's turn in a conversation.
senses.whyCN: 把声音拉长就填满了停顿，于是 oh 变成一个小工具，用来在对话里保住自己这一轮。

senses.title: Calling attention or adding emphasis
senses.definition: used before a name or remark to draw attention or to make the statement more emphatic
senses.definitionCN: 放在名字或话语前，用来引起注意或让语气更重
senses.example: Oh, Tom, the post has come.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，汤姆，邮件到了。
senses.why: The same cry that reacts to the world can be turned outward to reach another person, and there it works as a call.
senses.whyCN: 那声原本对世界作出反应的声音，也可以转向外去够到另一个人，这时它就起招呼的作用。

intro.en: Oh belongs to the small set of English exclamations that seem to come from the voice itself, and its exact origin is uncertain; what is recorded is its long life in speech and writing.
intro.cn: oh 属于英语中少数仿佛直接出自人声的感叹词，确切来源不确定；可考的是它在口语与书面语中长期存在。

items.en: A word of this kind is generally treated as a natural cry rather than a borrowing, so its earliest source is uncertain and no Latin parent can be named.
items.cn: 这类词一般认为属于人自然而发的叫声，而不是从某处借来，因此最早来源不确定，也指不出拉丁语祖先。

items.en: The interjection appears in early English writing as o or oo, used to call out, to mourn or to mark surprise.
items.cn: 这一感叹词在早期英语文献中写作 o 或 oo，用来呼唤、哀叹或表示惊讶。

items.en: By the sixteenth century oh was a common spelling, and it filled the stage with sighs, warnings and sudden turns of plot.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，oh 已是常见拼写，舞台上用它来叹气、示警或表示情节骤转。

items.en: Because the tone carries the meaning, the same oh can mark surprise, understanding, hesitation or distress without changing its shape.
items.cn: 因为意义由语调承载，同一个 oh 能表示惊讶、领会、迟疑或痛苦，而词形不变。

items.en: Modern English keeps oh for speech, letters and fiction, where it stands in for a sound rather than for a thing.
items.cn: 现代英语把 oh 留在口语、书信与小说里，它代替的是一个声音，而不是一件东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other short exclamations that look or sound close to oh; the near-meaning group collects interjections with overlapping emotional jobs.
note.cn: 形近组收其他拼写或发音与 oh 接近的短感叹词；近义组收情绪功能与之重叠的感叹词。

entries.definitionCN: 表示宽慰、疼痛或惊讶的短促开口声。

entries.definition: A two-part cry marking sudden understanding.

entries.definition: An old word expressing sorrow or regret.

entries.definition: A call used to attract attention or to greet.

normalIntro.en: Oh has no root to dig into; it is a sound that English wrote down, so the hooks follow the voice rather than a word family.
normalIntro.cn: oh 没有可挖掘的词根；它是英语记录下来的一个声音，所以记忆钩子顺着人声走，而不是顺着词族走。

normal.en: Oh has no parts and takes no endings, which places it outside the grammar of nouns and verbs.
normal.cn: oh 没有构件，也不接词尾，这使它落在名词与动词的语法之外。

normal.en: The voice decides the meaning: a rising oh asks, a flat oh acknowledges, a long oh hesitates.
normal.cn: 语调决定意思：上扬的 oh 在追问，平直的 oh 在应答，拖长的 oh 在迟疑。

normal.en: Oh dear and oh no borrow the sound for worry, while oh well borrows it for acceptance.
normal.cn: oh dear 与 oh no 借这个声音表示担忧，oh well 则借它表示接受。

normal.en: In writing, the comma after oh marks a pause that the voice would make anyway.
normal.cn: 书写时 oh 后面的逗号，标出的是人声本来就会有的停顿。

normal.en: Oh before a name turns the cry outward, which is why it can open a sentence addressed to someone.
normal.cn: oh 放在名字前，就把这声叫喊转向外，所以它能开启一句对某人说的话。

abstract.en: A word that is only a sound reminds us that language begins in breath before it settles into spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个只是声音的词提醒人：语言在落成拼写之前，先起于呼吸。

abstract.en: Oh can be surprise, agreement or delay because the listener reads the tone, not the letters.
abstract.cn: oh 能表示惊讶、同意或拖延，是因为听者读的是语调，不是字母。

abstract.en: Every conversation leaves a few of these small openings where feeling shows through.
abstract.cn: 每场对话都会留下几处这样的小缺口，情绪从中露出来。

examples.cn: 哦，火车又晚点了。

examples.en: Oh, mind the step at the door.

root: 来源不确定；一般认为这类感叹词由人自然发出的声音固定而成，与任何拉丁词根都没有派生关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open-mouthed sound of reaction; it branches into surprise, the reply that shows understanding, the drawn-out pause, and the call aimed at another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是遇事张口发出的一声；由此分出惊讶、表示明白的应答、拖长的停顿，以及冲着别人发出的招呼。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个人听到意外消息，嘴巴微张，一声短促的气从喉咙里出来。

definition_zh: 油；食用油；石油；润滑油；给……上油
definition_en: a thick liquid used for cooking or as fuel, a substance that keeps machinery sliding smoothly, and the verb meaning to put such a liquid on something
core_image: 一只陶罐的罐口挂着油珠，灯光下慢慢往下淌
scene: 厨房的灶台上摆着一只陶罐，罐口挂着金黄的油珠，旁边的铁锅正等着下菜。She poured a little oil into the hot pan.
sceneCN: 这里的 oil 是「食用油」（第 1 个义项：烹调用的油）；句意为她往热锅里倒了一点油。图中可辨识物件：陶罐、油珠、铁锅。

由 oil 加 -er 构成，义为「加油工；油轮」
由 oil 与 field 复合而成，义为「油田」

senses.title: A liquid fat used in cooking
senses.definition: a thick liquid made from plants or animals and used to cook or dress food
senses.definitionCN: 由植物或动物制成、用于烹调或拌食物的黏稠液体
senses.example: The salad was dressed with olive oil and lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 那份沙拉用橄榄油和柠檬调味。
senses.why: The oldest household use of the substance is in food, so the word begins with what sits in the kitchen jar.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质在家庭里最老的用途是入菜，所以这个词的起点就是厨房罐子里的东西。

senses.title: Petroleum extracted from the ground
senses.definition: the dark liquid pumped from beneath the earth and refined into fuel
senses.definitionCN: 从地下抽取、再炼成燃料的深色液体
senses.example: The country's economy depends on oil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的经济依赖石油。
senses.why: The same substance that fills a kitchen jar also fills pipelines, and industry simply kept the old word for the new scale.
senses.whyCN: 装满厨房罐子的同一种物质也装满管道，工业只是沿用了旧词，去说新的规模。

senses.title: A substance that reduces friction
senses.definition: a prepared liquid put between moving parts so that they slide without wearing
senses.definitionCN: 放在运动部件之间、让它们滑动而不磨损的调制液体
senses.example: The engine needs fresh oil every few thousand miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机每跑几千英里就要换新机油。
senses.why: Fat is slippery, so machines borrowed the kitchen word for the stuff that keeps metal from grinding.
senses.whyCN: 油脂是滑的，于是机器借用了厨房里的词，来指让金属不互相摩擦的东西。

senses.title: To put oil on something
senses.definition: to spread or apply oil to a surface, especially to keep it smooth or working
senses.definitionCN: 把油涂到某个表面上，尤指为了让它顺滑或保持运转
senses.example: He oiled the hinges so the gate would stop creaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他给铰链上了油，好让大门不再吱吱响。
senses.why: Once a noun names the substance, the verb can name the act of putting it on, and the object tells you which kind of oil is meant.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指这种物质，动词就能指把油涂上去的动作，而宾语则说明用的是哪一种油。

intro.en: Oil reached English from Old French, which had shortened a Latin word for olive oil; the Greek ancestor of that word is generally taken as the wider source of the family.
intro.cn: oil 经古法语进入英语，而古法语缩短了拉丁语中表示橄榄油的词；一般认为该词的希腊语祖先才是这一族词更早的来源。

items.en: The Greek word elaion named olive oil, and it is generally taken as the source of the wider family of oil words.
items.cn: 希腊语 elaion 指橄榄油，一般认为它是这一族油类词汇更早的来源。

items.en: Latin took the idea as oleum, oil, and kept oliva for the olive itself, so fruit and product had separate names.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 oleum 表示油，同时用 oliva 表示橄榄本身，果实与产物各有名字。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin form to oile and passed it into English speech after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形式缩短为 oile，在诺曼时期之后传入英语口语。

items.en: Middle English oile, later oil, covered cooking fat, lamp fuel and the greasy stuff used on tools.
items.cn: 中古英语的 oile（后作 oil）已兼指食用的油、点灯的油，以及涂在工具上的油脂。

items.en: Modern English extends oil to petroleum, to machine lubricants and to the verb of applying them.
items.cn: 现代英语把 oil 扩展到石油、机器润滑油，以及「涂抹这些油」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the oil stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for oily, greasy and fuelling substances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 oil 词干上的词；近义组收其他表示油性、油脂与燃料物质的名称。

entries.definition: Covered with oil, or tasting and feeling like oil.
entries.definitionCN: 沾满油的，或味道与触感像油的。

entries.definition: A person or device that oils machinery, or a ship carrying oil.
entries.definitionCN: 给机器上油的人或装置，也指运油的船。

entries.definition: An area where petroleum is drilled and pumped.
entries.definitionCN: 开采与抽取石油的区域。

entries.definition: A former name for margarine, built on the Latin word for oil.
entries.definitionCN: 人造黄油旧称，建立在拉丁语「油」一词上。

entries.definition: The mineral oil from which fuels and plastics are made.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制取燃料与塑料的矿物油。

entries.definition: Thick animal fat or a heavy lubricant.
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠的动物脂肪或重型润滑脂。

entries.definition: Any substance that reduces friction between surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能减少表面之间摩擦的物质。

entries.definition: Material burned to produce heat or power.
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧以产生热量或动力的物质。

normalIntro.en: Oil names the substance before it names any use, and its family grows by describing what is oily, who oils, and where oil is found.
normalIntro.cn: oil 先指这种物质，再指各种用途；词族靠描述「油性的」「上油的人」和「出油的地方」生长。

normal.en: Oil is a short noun with a long history: Greek elaion, Latin oleum, Old French oile, then English oil.
normal.cn: oil 是个短名词，却来历很长：希腊语 elaion、拉丁语 oleum、古法语 oile，再到英语 oil。

normal.en: Oily is oil plus -y, the suffix that turns a substance into a quality.
normal.cn: oily 是 oil 加 -y，这个后缀把一种物质变成一种性质。

normal.en: Oiler adds -er, so it names the person or device that does the oiling.
normal.cn: oiler 加 -er，因此指上油的人或装置。

normal.en: Oilfield is a compound: the field is where the oil is, not what it is made of.
normal.cn: oilfield 是复合词：field 指油所在的地方，而不是油由什么做成。

normal.en: The verb oil keeps the same shape, so oiled hinges and oiling a gate show the act without a new spelling.
normal.cn: 动词 oil 形态不变，所以 oiled hinges 与 oiling a gate 直接用原形加词尾表示动作。

abstract.en: One word for food, fuel and lubricant suggests that what matters is the slipperiness, not the purpose.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指食物、燃料与润滑剂，说明关键在「滑」，而不在用途。

abstract.en: Oil is ancient sunlight stored in liquid, which is why the same word can feed a kitchen and drive a nation.
abstract.cn: 石油是储存在液体里的远古阳光，所以同一个词既能养一间厨房，也能驱动一个国家。

abstract.en: To oil something is to make the world move more quietly, one hinge at a time.
abstract.cn: 给东西上油，就是让世界更安静地转动，一次一个铰链。

examples.en: A drop of oil fell from the jar onto the table.
examples.cn: 一滴油从罐子落到桌上。

examples.en: The truck carries crude oil from the port each night.
examples.cn: 卡车每晚从港口运走原油。

examples.en: He oiled the gate before the winter rains came.
examples.cn: 冬雨来临前他给大门上了油。

latinIntro.en: Latin oleum, oliva and oleosus are recorded, so the English family has a reliable Latin ancestry even though the earliest form is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oleum、oliva、oleosus 均有记录，所以尽管最早的形式来自希腊语，这一族英语词仍有可靠的拉丁语世系。

scene: 办公室的灯还亮着，编辑把打印稿铺在桌上，逐行核对后又用笔尖划去其中一行名字。One name was omitted from the final list.

senses.title: Leaving something out on purpose
senses.definition: to leave out a word, detail or step deliberately, so that it is not included
senses.definitionCN: 有意不把某个词、细节或步骤放进去，使其不被包含在内
senses.example: The editor omitted the last paragraph to save space.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了最后一段以节省篇幅。
senses.why: Latin omittere meant to let go or let pass, so leaving something out is pictured as releasing it rather than destroying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 omittere 意为放走、让过去，所以「省去」被想成把东西放开，而不是把它毁掉。

senses.title: Leaving something out by mistake
senses.definition: to fail to include or do something because one forgot or overlooked it
senses.definitionCN: 因为忘记或看漏而没有把某事列入或没有去做
senses.example: Two names were omitted from the guest list by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 有两个名字被无意中漏在了宾客名单之外。
senses.why: The same act of letting something pass can happen with or without intent, and English keeps one verb for both the planned and the accidental gap.
senses.whyCN: 同样一个「让它过去」的动作，可能有意也可能无意，英语用同一个动词兼指计划中的空缺和疏忽造成的空缺。

senses.title: Saying nothing about something
senses.definition: to say nothing about something, whether from carelessness or from a wish to avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 对某事一字不提，不论是出于疏忽还是有意回避
senses.example: He omitted any mention of the delay in his report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报告里对延误只字未提。
senses.why: If a word can be left out of a text, it can also be left out of speech, so the verb comes to mean passing over a matter in silence.
senses.whyCN: 一个词能从文本里省掉，也能从话语里省掉，于是这个动词就表示对一件事沉默地略过。

senses.title: Keeping someone off a list or group
senses.definition: to leave a person or thing out of a set, list or team, often as a decision
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物排除在一套名单或队伍之外，常是经过决定的
senses.example: The coach omitted him from the squad for the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把他排除在决赛的队员名单之外。
senses.why: A list is a set of chosen items, and whatever is not chosen is let go, so omission becomes a quiet way of excluding.
senses.whyCN: 名单是一组被选中项，凡没被选中的就被放开，于是「省去」也成了一种安静的排除方式。

intro.en: Omit comes from Latin omittere, a verb built from a prefix meaning away and mittere, to send or let go; the idea of releasing something explains why the word covers both deliberate cuts and accidental gaps.
intro.cn: omit 来自拉丁语 omittere，由表示「离开」的前缀与 mittere（送出、放走）构成；「把东西放开」这个想法解释了它为何兼指有意删削与无意遗漏。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the moving force inside a large family of English verbs.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，为英语一大族动词提供了内在的「送出」力量。

items.en: Ob- plus mittere, worn down to om-, gave omittere, to let go or let pass by, and its participle stem was omiss-.
items.cn: ob- 与 mittere 合成并磨变为 om-，得到 omittere，意为放走、让过去，其分词词干为 omiss-。

items.en: Old French took the verb as ometre, meaning to leave out or to fail to do, and used it of words and duties alike.
items.cn: 古法语借作 ometre，意为略去、漏做，词与职责都能接。

items.en: Middle English adopted it as omitten, and the modern spelling omit replaced the older ending in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语作 omitten，到十六世纪现代拼写 omit 取代了旧词尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps omit for leaving out words, facts, steps and people, and doubles the t in omitted and omitting because the stress falls on the last syllable.
items.cn: 现代英语让 omit 承担略去词语、事实、步骤与人，并因重音落在末音节而在 omitted、omitting 中双写 t。

senses.example: I met her once at a conference in Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 我在上海的一次会议上见过她一面。
senses.why: The Old English form was a genitive of the word for one, so the count starts at a single occasion and stops there.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式是「一」这个词的属格，所以计数从单独一次开始，也就到此为止。

senses.title: At some time in the past
senses.definition: at an unspecified time in the past, especially a period that is now over
senses.definitionCN: 在过去某个不确定的时期，尤指已经结束的一段时光
senses.example: He once worked as a night guard in a paper mill.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾在造纸厂当过夜班保安。
senses.why: A single occasion placed far enough back in memory stops being a count and becomes a period that once existed, which is how the word turns into formerly.
senses.whyCN: 单独一次被推到记忆深处，就不再是计数，而成了曾经存在过的一段日子，词义于是转为「从前」。

senses.title: As soon as; at the moment that
senses.definition: as soon as something happens, something else happens or becomes true
senses.definitionCN: 某事刚一发生，另一件事就随之发生或成立
senses.example: Once the rain stopped, the whole street came out to dry its washing.
senses.exampleCN: 雨一停，整条街的人就出来晾衣服。
senses.why: The count shrinks to a single moment, and that moment of time becomes the hinge on which the next event turns.
senses.whyCN: 计数收窄到一个瞬间，而时间上的那一刻正成了下一件事转动的铰链。

senses.title: If ever; whenever a condition holds
senses.definition: used to introduce a condition: if something ever happens or is true, the main clause follows
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出条件：只要某事发生或成立，后面的结果就随之而来
senses.example: Once you sign the form, the offer cannot be withdrawn.
senses.exampleCN: 你一旦签了这张表，这个录用条件就不能撤回。
senses.why: From the moment that to provided that is a short step, because a single moment can also mark the point where a condition takes effect.
senses.whyCN: 从「就在那一刻」到「只要」只有一小步，因为单独的那一刻也可以标出条件开始生效的位置。

intro.en: Once is a frozen genitive of the Old English word for one, and it has kept the meaning of a single occasion for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: once 是古英语「一」这个词属格形式的凝固，一千多年来一直保留「一次」的含义。

items.en: The numeral an meant one, and its genitive anes meant of one, which is the source of the modern word.
items.cn: 数词 an 意为「一」，它的属格 anes 意为「之一的」，正是现代 once 的来源。

items.en: In early English anes worked as an adverb for one time, and its final s was gradually absorbed into the spoken form.
items.cn: 在早期英语中，anes 作副词表示「一次」，词尾的 s 逐渐被口语形式吸收。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as ones and once competed, and once won because it matched the pattern of twice.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ones 与 once 等拼法并存，once 最终胜出，因为它与 twice 的构词方式相合。

items.en: By the sixteenth century once had also become a conjunction meaning as soon as, turning a count of times into a point in time.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，once 又发展出连词用法，表示「一…就」，把次数扩展为时间上的一个点。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adverb of counting and the conjunction of condition, and once also lives inside fixed phrases such as at once and once more.
items.cn: 现代英语保留计数的副词与表条件的连词，once 也活在 at once、once more 这类固定短语里。

normalIntro.en: The word is a frozen count of one, and its family keeps returning to a single occasion, a single past period and a single moment that starts something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一」的凝固计数，同族用法反复回到单独一次、单独一段过去，以及开启某事的单独一刻。

normal.en: The Old English genitive anes meant of one, so once is literally a count of one occasion.
normal.cn: 古英语属格 anes 意为「之一的」，所以 once 字面上就是数一次。

normal.en: Once and twice share the ending -ce, which is why the two words sound like a matched pair.
normal.cn: once 与 twice 共用词尾 -ce，所以两个词听起来像成对的。

normal.en: At once means at one moment, and that is how a count turns into immediacy.
normal.cn: at once 意为「就在一刻」，计数就是这样转成「立刻」。

normal.en: Once as a conjunction marks the single moment when something begins, and English glosses it as as soon as.
normal.cn: once 作连词时标出某事开始的那一瞬间，英语用 as soon as 来解释它。

normal.en: For once stresses that the single occasion is unusual rather than the usual pattern.
normal.cn: for once 强调这一次不同寻常，而不是一贯如此。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket torn in half after one ride: the stub left in the box is the whole of the word once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张车票在一次行程后被撕成两半：留在盒里的票根就是 once 的全部含义。

abstract.en: A single second on a clock face can set everything else moving, and that second is once standing at the head of a clause.
abstract.cn: 钟面上单独的一秒能让之后的一切动起来，而这一秒就是站在小句开头的 once。

abstract.en: Memory turns one distant occasion into the softer word once, the way a photograph outlives the day it was taken.
abstract.cn: 记忆把遥远的一次变成语气更柔的 once，就像照片比拍摄的那一天活得更久。

definition_zh: 在线的；联网的；网上的；在网上；联网地
definition_en: connected to or available through a computer network, especially the internet; as an adverb, by means of such a connection
core_image: 一根细线从桌上的机器伸向看不见的远方，屏幕随即亮起别人的声音
scene: 深夜的书房里只剩屏幕的光，桌角那根网线轻轻闪着小灯。She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
sceneCN: 这里 online 是「在网上、联网地」（第 2 个义项：通过互联网进行某种活动）；句意是她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。画面是深夜的书房、亮着的屏幕与闪烁的网线指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「离开」的 off 与 line 复合，与 online 构成反义对，义为「离线的」
由 online 与 only 复合而成，义为「只在网上提供或经营的」

senses.title: Connected to a computer network
senses.definition: connected to a computer network or to the internet and able to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 接入计算机网络或互联网，能够交换数据
senses.example: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。
senses.why: Line first named a wire or a telephone connection, so being on that line is literally being attached to the network.
senses.whyCN: line 最初指一根导线或一条电话线，所谓「在这条线上」就是实实在在接在网络里。

senses.title: By means of an internet connection
senses.definition: by using an internet connection rather than a physical place or a paper form
senses.definitionCN: 借助互联网连接，而不是通过实体场所或纸质表格
senses.example: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。
senses.why: Once the line carries data, any action done through it can take the same word as an adverb of manner.
senses.whyCN: 当这条线传输的是数据，任何经由它完成的动作都能用同一个词作方式状语。

senses.title: Available or stored on the internet
senses.definition: existing, offered or stored on the internet, as opposed to a printed or physical version
senses.definitionCN: 存在于互联网上、在网上提供或保存的，与纸质或实体版本相对
senses.example: The journal moved its whole archive online last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家期刊去年把全部过刊搬到了网上。
senses.why: The adjective then moves from the connected machine to the thing that can only be reached through that connection.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词于是从「联网的机器」转到「只能通过网络抵达的内容」。

intro.en: Online joins the old noun line with the preposition on, and its modern life began with telephone wires before it passed to computer networks.
intro.cn: online 把古老的名词 line 与介词 on 合在一起，它的现代生命先始于电话线，随后转到计算机网络。

items.en: Linea meant a thread of flax and then any straight cord, and it is the source of the English noun line.
items.cn: linea 原指一根亚麻线，后来泛指任何笔直的绳索，是英语名词 line 的来源。

items.en: Old English borrowed line for a rope or a cord, and the word later also meant a row and a boundary.
items.cn: 古英语借入 line 表示绳索，这个词后来又指一排、一行以及一条界线。

items.en: In the nineteenth century a line was the wire joining two telephones, and being on the line meant being connected.
items.cn: 十九世纪，line 指连接两台电话的导线，「在线上」就意味着接通。

items.en: With computer networks the line became a data connection, and online was formed for equipment attached to it.
items.cn: 到了计算机网络时期，这条线变成数据连接，online 随之造出，用来形容接入其中的设备。

items.en: Modern English extends online from the connected device to the activity performed through it and to the content kept there.
items.cn: 现代英语把 online 从「接通的设备」扩展到「经由它完成的活动」与「存放在其中的内容」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the opposite form and other compounds built on line; the near-meaning group gathers words about networks and electronic access.
note.cn: 形近组收它的反义形式以及同样以 line 构成的复合词；近义组收表示网络与电子访问的词。

entries.definition: Not connected to a network, built with off- in place of on-.
entries.definitionCN: 不接入网络的，用 off- 替换 on- 构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: The noun at the centre of the compound, meaning a cord, a row or a connection.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中心的名词，意为绳索、一排或一条连接。

entries.definition: Placed within a line of text, a different compound with the same second element.
entries.definitionCN: 排在文本行内的，第二个成分相同，但整体是另一个复合词。

entries.definition: The outer edge of a shape or a short summary; it shares line but not the meaning of connection.
entries.definitionCN: 形状的外缘或简要提纲；同含 line，但不表示连接。

entries.definition: Joined to a network or to another device.
entries.definitionCN: 接入网络或与另一设备相连的。

entries.definition: Stored or carried as electronic data rather than on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 以电子数据而非纸质方式存储或传输的。

entries.definition: Existing on computers or networks rather than in a physical place.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于计算机或网络中而不是实体场所的。

entries.definition: Accessed from a distance, usually through a network.
entries.definitionCN: 从远处访问的，通常经由网络。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures a machine attached to a line, and its family keeps the same thin thread running between a room and the world outside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘一台接在一条线上的机器，同族用法始终保留那根从房间伸向外界的细线。

normal.en: Line came from Latin linea, a thread, so online inherits the picture of a cord.
normal.cn: line 来自拉丁语 linea（线），所以 online 继承了「一根绳线」的画面。

normal.en: On adds the idea of being attached to or supported by that cord.
normal.cn: on 加上「附着于、由它支撑」的意思。

normal.en: Offline replaces on with off and marks a machine that has stepped away from the network.
normal.cn: offline 用 off 替换 on，标出已经离开网络的机器。

normal.en: Telephone lines gave the word its first everyday use, long before computers arrived.
normal.cn: 电话线给了这个词最早的日常用法，远在计算机出现之前。

normal.en: Online course and online shopping show the same word spreading to study and to trade.
normal.cn: online course 与 online shopping 说明同一个词又扩展到了学习与买卖。

abstract.en: Picture a single cable running out of a lit room into the dark: whatever waits at the other end becomes present on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从亮着灯的屋子伸进黑暗：另一头的一切都会出现在屏幕上。

abstract.en: Being online means the walls of the room no longer decide what you can reach.
abstract.cn: 「在线」意味着房间的墙不再决定你能触及什么。

abstract.en: The same word covers the wire, the act and the content, because a connection quietly turns into a place.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了线路、动作与内容，因为一条连接会悄悄变成一个场所。

examples.en: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
examples.cn: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。

examples.en: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
examples.cn: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。

examples.en: Most of the course materials are now online.
examples.cn: 大部分课程材料现在都在网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，来网」——哦，网来了，人就上线了；online 意为在线的、上网的。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a machine attached to a line; the senses move from the connected device to the action performed through it and to the material kept there.

branches.cn: 打印机上的小灯转绿

definition_zh: 只；仅仅；唯一；只有；不过
definition_en: and nothing or nobody else; no more than; single and without a second one; but, used to introduce a drawback
core_image: 一排同样的杯子被逐个搬走，只有一个留在原来的位置
scene: 仓库清点那天，货架上成排的水杯被一件件搬走，最后只剩一只留在原来的位置。Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
sceneCN: 这里 only 是「唯一的、仅剩的」（第 2 个义项：同类中只有一个）；句意是清点之后货架上只剩一只杯子。画面是空了大半的货架与孤零零的一只杯子。

derivatives.zh: 由 only 与 child 组成的固定说法，义为「独生子女」
由 only 与 begotten 复合而成的古语，义为「独生的；唯一的」
由 only 的词基 one 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「一体；同一性」

senses.title: No more than; and nothing else
senses.definition: no more than a particular number, amount or thing, and nothing in addition
senses.definitionCN: 不超过某个数目、数量或事物，此外再无别的
senses.example: She packed only a small bag for the whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 整整一周她只收拾了一个小包。
senses.why: The word is one plus -ly, and its job is to cut a set down to a single member, so the sense begins as a limit on quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 one 加 -ly 构成，职责是把一个集合削减到单独一个成员，所以词义从「限量」开始。

senses.title: Single and without another
senses.definition: being the single one of its kind, with no second one to choose from
senses.definitionCN: 同类之中只有一个，没有第二个可供选择
senses.example: Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
senses.exampleCN: 清点之后，货架上只剩一只杯子。
senses.why: When the same limit is applied to a whole group, the member left is the sole one, and the adverb turns into an adjective of uniqueness.
senses.whyCN: 把同样的限量用在整个群体上，剩下的那一个就成了唯一者，副词于是变成表「唯一」的形容词。

senses.title: Solely, marking the single person or thing that qualifies
senses.definition: used to say that a particular person or thing is the only one that does something or is allowed to do it
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某人或某物是唯一做某事或获准做某事的一个
senses.example: Only the manager can open that safe.
senses.exampleCN: 只有经理才能打开那个保险柜。
senses.why: Here the cut falls on the doers rather than on the quantity, so the word points at the single agent allowed to act.
senses.whyCN: 这里的削减落在做事的人而不是数量上，所以这个词指向唯一获准行动的那个主体。

senses.title: But; except that
senses.definition: used before a fact that makes what was just said less strong or less happy
senses.definitionCN: 用在某个使前文减弱或令人不那么愉快的事实之前
senses.example: The flat is cheap, only it is far from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这套房子便宜，只不过离车站太远。
senses.why: A limit on goodness is still a limit, so the same cutting word comes to mark the one flaw that a praise has to admit.
senses.whyCN: 对「好处」加以限制仍然是限制，于是这个表示削减的词转来标出称赞不得不承认的那一处缺陷。

intro.en: Only is one plus the suffix -ly, and it grew from a numeral into a word that limits, singles out and finally concedes.
intro.cn: only 由「一」加后缀 -ly 构成，从数词长成一个表示限量、挑出唯一者、最后表示让步的词。

items.en: The adjective anlic meant one-like or alone, built from an, one, and -lic, the ancestor of -ly.
items.cn: 形容词 anlic 意为「像一的、单独的」，由 an（一）与 -lic（-ly 的前身）构成。

items.en: The adverb anlice limited a statement to a single item, and its spoken form gradually shrank toward only.
items.cn: 副词 anlice 把陈述限制在单独一项上，它的口语形式逐渐缩减为 only。

items.en: Middle English only served both as adjective and adverb, meaning alone, single and no more than.
items.cn: 中古英语的 only 兼作形容词与副词，意为单独的、唯一的、仅仅。

items.en: Later the word gained a concessive use before clauses of objection, as in it is cheap, only it is far.
items.cn: 后来这个词又在表示异议的小句前获得让步用法，如「便宜，只不过太远」。

items.en: Modern English uses only for quantity, for uniqueness, for a single qualifying person, and for a mild objection.
items.cn: 现代英语用 only 表示数量限制、唯一性、唯一符合条件者，以及温和的反对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same one-plus-suffix pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words of limitation and singleness.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由「一」加后缀构成的词；近义组收表示限制与单独的词语。

entries.definition: The numeral inside only, still meaning a single thing or person.
entries.definitionCN: only 内部那个数词，至今表示单独的一件或一人。

entries.definition: Built in origin on the same one-plus pattern, meaning without others.
entries.definitionCN: 来源上同样由「一」加后缀构成，意为独自、没有别人。

entries.definition: From alone plus -ly, meaning sad at being without company; the spelling is close but the history differs.
entries.definitionCN: 由 alone 加 -ly 构成，意为孤独的；拼写相近，但构词历史不同。

entries.definition: Another adverb built from one, meaning one time; it sounds close but marks a count rather than a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由「一」构成的副词，意为一次；读音相近，但标的是次数而非限量。

entries.definition: Only and nothing more, used to play down what is described.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、只不过，用来淡化所描述的事物。

entries.definition: Exactly, or only; often interchangeable with only in limits.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好、仅仅；在表示限制时常可与 only 互换。

entries.definition: For one reason or by one person alone.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅因为一个原因，或只由一个人。

entries.definition: Single and the only one existing.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的；唯一存在的。

normalIntro.en: The word leaves a single item in view, and its family keeps narrowing a shelf, a group and a sentence down to one member.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只把一个物件留在视野里，同族用法一再把货架、群体与句子收窄到一个成员。

normal.en: Only is one plus -ly, so its oldest job is to leave a single item in view.
normal.cn: only 是 one 加 -ly，最古老的任务就是只留一个物件在视野里。

normal.en: Alone and lonely share the same one-plus-suffix origin, which is why all three suggest being by oneself.
normal.cn: alone 与 lonely 共用「一」加后缀的来源，所以三者都带「独自」的意味。

normal.en: Only the manager limits the doers, while only a small bag limits the quantity.
normal.cn: only the manager 限制的是做事的人，only a small bag 限制的是数量。

normal.en: Not only opens a set instead of closing it, which is why it pairs with but also.
normal.cn: not only 不是关上一个集合，而是把它打开，所以要与 but also 配合。

normal.en: The concessive only, as in only it is far, marks the single flaw left in a praise.
normal.cn: 表示让步的 only，如 only it is far，标出称赞里剩下的那一处缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical cups and all but one carried away: the survivor is the thing only points at.
abstract.cn: 想象一货架同样的杯子只只被搬走，只剩一只：留下来的那只就是 only 所指的东西。

abstract.en: A spotlight narrowed to one face explains the word better than a definition, because everything else simply falls outside the beam.
abstract.cn: 把聚光灯收窄到一张脸上，比任何定义都更能解释这个词，因为其余一切都落在光束之外。

abstract.en: The same narrowing falls on a number, a person or a good quality, which is why one small word serves four jobs.
abstract.cn: 同一种收窄可以落在数量、某个人或某处好处上，所以这一个小词能担四项职责。

examples.en: She packed only a small bag for the whole week.
examples.cn: 整整一周她只收拾了一个小包。

examples.en: Only the manager can open that safe.
examples.cn: 只有经理才能打开那个保险柜。

examples.en: The flat is cheap, only it is far from the station.
examples.cn: 这套房子便宜，只不过离车站太远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂立」——昂首立着的只有一个；only 意为只、唯一的。

root: 古英语 anlic（像一的、单独的）由 an（一）加 -lic（-ly 的前身）构成，副词 anlice 逐渐缩为 only；词义从「单独」发展为「只、仅仅、唯一」，再引申出「不过」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is narrowing a set to one; the senses apply that narrowing to quantity, to uniqueness, to the single qualifying agent, and finally to a single flaw.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一个集合收窄到一个」；义项把这层收窄依次用在数量、唯一性、唯一符合条件的主体，最后用在一处缺陷上。

core.cn: 核心意象：一排同样的杯子，除了一只之外都被搬走。

definition_zh: 到…上面；向…之上；转到（话题）；发觉（线索）
definition_en: moving to a position on the surface of something; also used for boarding, for turning to a new subject, and for being on the track of something
core_image: 一只手把杯子从一张桌子提起，又稳稳放到另一张桌子上
scene: 厨房里，端着热汤的人侧身走过，把碗从灶台挪到餐桌中央。He lifted the hot pot onto the middle of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 onto 是「到…上面」（第 1 个义项：移动到某物的表面之上）；句意是他把热锅端到桌子中央。画面是灶台、餐桌与冒着热气的锅。

pos.zh: 到…上面；向…之上；转到（话题）；发觉（线索）

derivatives.zh: 与 onto 同样由「介词加 to」构成，义为「到…里面」
由 on 与 to 演变而来的古旧形式，义为「到；向」
由 there 与 on 复合而成的正式副词，义为「在其上」

senses.title: To a position on a surface
senses.definition: moving so as to be on the surface of something or supported by it
senses.definitionCN: 移动之后位于某物表面之上，或由它支撑
senses.example: He lifted the hot pot onto the middle of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把热锅端到桌子中央。
senses.why: Onto is on plus to, so it keeps both the direction of to and the contact of on: the movement ends on a surface.
senses.whyCN: onto 由 on 加 to 构成，同时保留 to 的「去向」与 on 的「接触」，即移动终点落在某个表面上。

senses.title: Up to a vehicle or a raised place
senses.definition: used with verbs of climbing or boarding, to show getting on a vehicle, a horse or a higher place
senses.definitionCN: 与攀爬、乘坐类动词连用，表示登上交通工具、马匹或高处
senses.example: The boy climbed onto the roof to fetch the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩爬上屋顶去取球。
senses.why: A vehicle and a roof are surfaces raised above the ground, so the surface sense narrows to getting up on them.
senses.whyCN: 交通工具和屋顶都是高过地面的表面，于是「表面」义收窄为「登上它们」的动作。

senses.title: Concerning; starting to deal with
senses.definition: used with verbs such as move or get, to show that someone starts talking about or dealing with a new subject
senses.definitionCN: 与 move、get 等动词连用，表示开始谈论或处理一个新话题
senses.example: Let us move onto the next question before we run out of time.
senses.exampleCN: 趁时间还没用完，我们接着谈下一个问题吧。
senses.why: The picture of stepping from one surface to another is reused for stepping from one topic to the next, so progress becomes movement.
senses.whyCN: 「从一块表面踏到另一块」的画面被移用到话题之间，于是推进被说成移动。

senses.title: Aware of something hidden; on the track of
senses.definition: used in be onto something, meaning to have discovered something important or to suspect someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be onto something，表示发现了重要线索或对某人起了疑心
senses.example: The researchers may be onto a cheaper way of storing solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 这些研究者可能发现了储存太阳能的一种更便宜的办法。
senses.why: If a trail or a scent is imagined as a surface, finding it means standing on it, which is why discovery is phrased as being onto something.
senses.whyCN: 如果把踪迹或气味想象成一块表面，找到它就等于站到了上面，所以「发现」被说成 be onto something。

intro.en: Onto is a young preposition made by joining two older ones, and its written form appears only after on and to had long lived apart.
intro.cn: onto 是一个年轻的介词，由两个更古老的介词合并而成，它的书写形式在 on 与 to 分开使用很久之后才出现。

items.en: On came from Old English an, meaning in or upon, and it named contact and support.
items.cn: on 源自古英语 an，意为在…之中、在…之上，指接触与支撑。

items.en: To came from Old English to, meaning toward a place, and it named direction and a destination.
items.cn: to 源自古英语 to，意为朝某处，指方向与目的地。

items.en: Middle English kept on and to apart, and wrote on to as two words when movement and contact had to be shown at once.
items.cn: 中古英语把 on 与 to 分开使用，需要同时表示移动与接触时就写作 on to 两个词。

items.en: The single written form onto appears in the eighteenth century, generally considered a blending of the two words, though many writers still prefer on to.
items.cn: 一般认为单一拼写 onto 出现在十八世纪，由两个词合并而成，但不少作者仍偏向写作 on to。

items.en: Modern English uses onto for physical movement, for boarding, for a new topic and for being on the track of something.
items.cn: 现代英语用 onto 表示实体移动、登上交通工具、转向新话题，以及察觉到某事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers prepositions built on the same on-plus-to pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words of position above or on something.
note.cn: 形近组收同样按「on 加 to」模式构成的介词；近义组收表示在某物之上或更高位置的词。

entries.definition: An older form of to, formed with on or un; it looks close but is not the modern onto.
entries.definitionCN: to 的一种较古形式，由 on 或 un 构成；形近，但不是现代的 onto。

entries.definition: A formal adverb meaning on that or on it, built from there plus on.
entries.definitionCN: 正式副词，意为「在其上」，由 there 加 on 构成。

entries.definition: On or onto, especially in formal and literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 在…之上或到…之上，尤用于正式与文学语体。

entries.definition: On top of something.

entries.definition: In a higher position than something, without the idea of contact.
entries.definitionCN: 位置高于某物，不含接触之意。

entries.definition: Towards a higher place or position.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更高的地方或位置。

normalIntro.en: The word fuses contact with direction, and its family keeps the picture of a hand carrying something until it rests on a new surface.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把接触与方向合在一起，同族用法始终保留「一只手把东西搬过去，直到落在新表面上」的画面。

normal.en: Onto is on plus to, so it fuses contact with direction in one short word.
normal.cn: onto 是 on 加 to，用一个短词把接触与方向合在一起。

normal.en: Into follows the same pattern with in, which is why the two prepositions are usually learned together.
normal.cn: into 用 in 走同样的路子，所以这两个介词常被一起学。

normal.en: Boarding a bus or a horse falls under onto because both are raised surfaces.
normal.cn: 上公交车或上马都用 onto，因为二者都是高起的表面。

normal.en: Move onto a new topic borrows the physical step from one surface to another.
normal.cn: move onto a new topic 借用了从一块表面踏到另一块的动作。

normal.en: Hold onto keeps the contact and adds the effort of not letting go.
normal.cn: hold onto 保留接触之意，又加上「不松手」的用力。

abstract.en: Picture a cup lifted from a counter and set down on another table: the arc of the hand is the to, the landing is the on.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子从台面提起又落到另一张桌上：手的弧线是 to，落点是 on。

abstract.en: Every new subject is a new surface to stand on, which is why progress and conversation share one preposition.
abstract.cn: 每个新话题都是一块可站的新表面，所以推进与谈话共用同一个介词。

abstract.en: Being onto something means the trail is under your feet, even when nothing can be seen yet.
abstract.cn: be onto something 意味着踪迹已经在脚下，尽管此时还什么都看不见。

examples.cn: 他把热锅端到桌子中央。

examples.cn: 男孩爬上屋顶去取球。

examples.en: The researchers may be onto a cheaper way of storing solar power.

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一次以落在表面为终点的移动」；义项把这层落点扩展到交通工具、新话题，以及发现线索时脚下的落点。

definition_zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地
definition_en: in a way that does not hide facts, feelings or intentions and can be seen or heard by other people
core_image: 一扇原本关着的窗被推开，屋里的东西全暴露在日光下
scene: 会议进行到一半，一位年轻工程师站起来，把项目失败的原因一条条讲出来，没有替任何人遮掩。He spoke openly about the delays that had ruined the schedule.
sceneCN: 这里是「公开地、不隐瞒地」（第 1 个义项：不掩饰事实或态度）；句意为他把拖垮进度的延误坦然讲了出来。图中可辨识物件：推开的窗、照进屋内的日光、摊开的文件。

pos.zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 open 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「公开；坦率；开阔」
由动词 open 加 -ing 构成，义为「开口；开幕；空缺职位」
由 open 加表示「做某事的人或物」的 -er 构成，义为「开启者；开瓶器」

senses.title: Without hiding the facts
senses.definition: in a way that lets other people see or know the facts instead of keeping them secret
senses.definitionCN: 让他人看到或知道事实，而不是把事实藏起来
senses.example: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她公开承认初稿失败了。
senses.why: Open describes something not shut and not covered, so acting openly means leaving the facts uncovered for anyone to look at.
senses.whyCN: open 形容没有关闭、没有遮盖的东西，所以 openly 做事就是把事实摊开任人查看，而不是盖上一块布。

senses.title: In front of other people
senses.definition: in public, where other people can see or hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合，别人能够看见或听见所发生的事
senses.example: The two ministers openly disagreed in front of the press.
senses.exampleCN: 两位部长在记者面前公开表示意见不合。
senses.why: If nothing is covered, the act cannot stay private, so the same picture of an open space turns into doing something in public.
senses.whyCN: 既然没有遮盖，这个动作就留不住私密性；同一种「空间敞开」的画面，自然转到「当众做事」的含义上。

senses.title: Frankly, with feelings shown
senses.definition: in a direct way that shows real feelings or intentions without disguise
senses.definitionCN: 直接表达真实情感或意图，不加伪装
senses.example: They openly wept when the old theatre was pulled down.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老剧院被拆时，他们毫不掩饰地哭了。
senses.why: The image stretches from objects to feelings: a face that hides nothing is as open as a door that has never been locked.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象从物体延伸到情感：一张不藏东西的脸，就像一扇从没上过锁的门那样「敞开」。

intro.en: Openly is the adjective open plus the adverb suffix -ly, so its history is the history of open, a native English and Germanic word rather than a Latin one.
intro.cn: openly 就是形容词 open 加副词后缀 -ly，它的历史就是 open 的历史，而 open 是英语本土的日耳曼词，并非来自拉丁语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *upanaz is generally tied to the idea of being up or lifted, and it is the source of the English word for not shut.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *upanaz 与「向上、抬起」的意思相关，是英语中表示「未关闭」这个词的来源。

items.en: Old English already had open as an adjective for what is not closed, not covered or not blocked.
items.cn: 古英语里已有 open 这个形容词，表示未关闭、未遮盖或未被阻挡。

items.en: Middle English added -ly to adjectives to build adverbs, and openly appeared as the manner word for open action.
items.cn: 中古英语用 -ly 把形容词变成副词，openly 就这样出现，表示「以敞开的方式」。

items.en: The adverb moved from physical openings to speech, so saying something openly meant saying it with nothing concealed.
items.cn: 这个副词从物理上的敞开扩展到言语，说某事 openly 就是一点不隐瞒地说。

items.en: Modern English uses openly mainly for facts, feelings and public disagreement, and speak openly has become the usual pairing.
items.cn: 现代英语的 openly 主要用于事实、情感和公开的分歧，speak openly 已成为最常见的搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the open family and its spellings; the near-meaning group keeps adverbs that describe how plainly something is said or done.
note.cn: 形近组收 open 词族的同根词与不同拼写；近义组收同样描述「说得或做得有多直白」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind openly, meaning not closed and not hidden.
entries.definitionCN: openly 所由构成的形容词，义为未关闭、不隐瞒的。

entries.definition: A hole or gap, or the first performance of a show.
entries.definitionCN: 开口或缺口的；也指演出的首场。

entries.definition: The quality of being open, honest or free to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 公开、坦诚或可自由进入的性质。

entries.definition: Generous, with the hand open to give.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨大方的，手掌张开愿意给予。

entries.definition: In a direct and honest way, with no attempt to hide anything.
entries.definitionCN: 直接而诚实，不试图隐瞒任何东西。

entries.definition: In a place or manner that everyone can see or know.
entries.definitionCN: 在人人可见可知的场合或方式下。

entries.definition: Honestly, even when the truth makes people uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实地说，即使真相让人不舒服。

normalIntro.en: The word is open plus -ly, so every mnemonic hangs on the picture of something uncovered and on the small family built from the same adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 open 加 -ly，所以联想都围绕「没有遮盖」的画面，以及由同一形容词长出的那一小族词。

normal.en: Open means not shut, so openly means with nothing shut away.
normal.cn: open 是「没关上」，openly 就是「没把任何东西关起来藏住」。

normal.en: -ly turns the adjective into a manner, so an open act becomes an act done openly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词变成方式，于是 open 的动作就成了 openly 地做。

normal.en: Openness is the noun of the same family, naming the same quality as a thing.
normal.cn: openness 是同一词族的名词形式，把同一种性质当成一个东西来说。

normal.en: An opening is the place where something has been opened: a gap or a first night.
normal.cn: opening 是被打开的地方：一个缺口，或一场首演。

normal.en: Speak openly is the most common pairing, because speech is where hiding is easiest.
normal.cn: speak openly 是最常见的搭配，因为言语最容易把东西藏住。

abstract.en: A window pushed up in the morning: the room has nothing left to hide.
abstract.cn: 清晨把窗子推上去：屋子再没有可以藏的东西。

abstract.en: A closed hand keeps a secret, while an open hand must show what it holds.
abstract.cn: 握紧的手能藏住秘密，张开的手只能让人看见掌心里的东西。

abstract.en: Saying a hard truth openly costs more than saying an easy one quietly.
abstract.cn: 把难听的真相公开说出来，比轻声说一句好听话代价更大。

examples.en: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
examples.cn: 她公开承认初稿失败了。

examples.en: The committee openly rejected the proposal.
examples.cn: 委员会公开否决了这项提议。

examples.en: He prefers to speak openly rather than hint at problems.
examples.cn: 他宁愿把问题直说，也不愿只做暗示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧盆里」——盆盖一掀开，里面的东西全看得见；记住 openly 是公开地。

root: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，一般认为来自重构词根 *upanaz（向上、抬起）；加 -ly 构成副词 openly，义为「以敞开、不遮掩的方式」。这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an uncovered surface, and the senses move from facts that are not hidden, to acts done in public, to feelings shown without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有遮盖的表面」；义项从「不隐瞒的事实」移到「在人前做的事」，再到「不加伪装地流露情感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window pushed open so that everything inside stands in plain light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇被推开的窗，屋里的一切都摆在明处。

branches.en: a draft read aloud with the failed pages left in
branches.cn: 朗读稿子时把失败的页码照样留在里面

branches.en: a manager naming the delay instead of blaming the weather
branches.cn: 负责人直接点出延误，而不是怪天气

branches.en: two officials arguing in front of reporters
branches.cn: 两位官员在记者面前争论

branches.en: a face that will not look away while speaking
branches.cn: 说话时不肯把脸转开

branches.en: mourners weeping without turning aside
branches.cn: 送别的人不侧过脸就哭了出来

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for not shut plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the family around it adds nouns for the gap, the act and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「未关闭」的日耳曼语形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成；它周围的一族词再用名词形式表示缺口、动作与性质。

latinIntro.en: Open is native English and Germanic, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: not closed, not covered, not hidden
items.meaningCN: 未关闭的；未遮盖的；不隐瞒的
items.example: The door was left open all night.

items.meaning: in a way that hides nothing
items.exampleCN: 他们公开讨论了这次损失。

items.example: Her openness made the meeting shorter.
items.exampleCN: 她的坦率让会议开得更短。

items.meaning: a gap or a first performance
items.example: The opening drew a full house.

items.meaning: a person or tool that opens
items.example: He borrowed an opener for the bottle.
items.exampleCN: 他借了个开瓶器开瓶子。

items.example: The envelope stayed unopened for a week.

items.meaning: someone or something with nothing to hide
items.example: His finances are an open book.
items.exampleCN: 他的财务状况一目了然。

definition_zh: 歌剧；歌剧艺术；歌剧院；歌剧团
definition_en: a dramatic work set to music and sung by trained singers, usually with an orchestra, and also the art form or the house where it is staged
core_image: 歌唱者站在彩绘布景前，乐队在乐池里等最后一个音符落下
scene: 假期最后一晚，一家人换上正式衣服，走进河边那座老剧场，准备从头听到尾。The whole family dressed up to hear an opera that lasted four hours.
sceneCN: 这里是「歌剧作品」（第 1 个义项：谱成音乐、由歌手演唱的戏剧）；句意为一家人盛装去听一部长达四小时的歌剧。图中可辨识物件：舞台布景、乐池、观众席。

pos.zh: 歌剧；歌剧艺术；歌剧院；歌剧团

derivatives.zh: 由 opera 加 -ic 构成，义为「歌剧的；歌剧式的」
意大利语 operetta 是 opera 的指小形式，义为「轻歌剧」
直接来自拉丁语 opus（作品），与 opera 同出一源，义为「作品；乐曲」

senses.title: A drama sung on stage
senses.definition: a play set to music, in which the story is told through singing rather than ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 谱成音乐的戏剧，故事用歌唱而不是日常说话来讲
senses.example: The new opera was written by a young composer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。
senses.why: Latin opera is the plural of opus, a work; Italian took it for a musical work, and English borrowed that name for the kind of drama that is sung.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opera 是 opus（作品）的复数；意大利语借它指「谱成音乐的作品」，英语再借来，就成了这类唱着演的戏剧的名字。

senses.title: The art form itself
senses.titleCN: 歌剧艺术；歌剧这一体裁
senses.definition: the art form or genre of such works, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把这类作品作为整体来看的艺术形式或门类
senses.example: She has spent thirty years in opera.
senses.exampleCN: 她在歌剧这一行干了三十年。
senses.why: Once it names individual works, the word can name the whole field those works belong to, just as a kind of object can give its name to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 既然能指一部部作品，也就能指这些作品所属的整个领域；就像某类物件可以给出一个行当的名字。

senses.title: The building or the company
senses.definition: the theatre, or the company, where such works are staged
senses.definitionCN: 上演这类作品的剧院，或经营它的团体
senses.example: The opera is rebuilding its stage this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 歌剧院今年冬天要重修它的舞台。
senses.why: A place or an institution often takes the name of the art it presents, so the word moves from the work to the house that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 演出场所或团体常直接拿它所演的艺术来命名，词义就从「作品」转到「上演作品的房子」。

intro.en: Opera reached English through Italian, but behind it sits the Latin word for a work; its family includes opus and operatic, not the separate verb for working.
intro.cn: opera 经意大利语进入英语，背后却是拉丁语中「作品」这个词；同族词包括 opus 与 operatic，而不包括另一个表示「干活」的动词。

items.en: Latin opus meant work, effort or a product, and its plural opera meant works; the genitive operis keeps the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作、出力或成果，复数 opera 指多件作品；属格 operis 保留同一词干。

items.en: In Latin, opera could already name a work of art, and the phrase opera in musica named a work set to music.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中 opera 已经可以指一件艺术品，短语 opera in musica 专指「谱成音乐的作品」。

items.en: Italian composers and audiences made opera the name of the new sung drama, and that sense became fixed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的意大利作曲家与观众拿 opera 当作这种新的歌唱戏剧的名字，词义就此固定下来。

items.en: English borrowed the Italian word and soon used it for the building where such works were staged, giving opera house.
items.cn: 英语借入这个意大利词，很快又用它指上演这类作品的建筑，于是有了 opera house。

items.en: Modern English keeps the musical sense and loosens it in soap opera, where the link is serial drama rather than song.
items.cn: 现代英语保留音乐戏剧的含义，并在 soap opera 里把这种联系放宽到长篇连续剧，与歌唱无关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin words for a work and the operatic family; the near-meaning group gathers other staged or sung arts.
note.cn: 形近组收与「作品」有关、来自拉丁语的同族词；近义组收其他舞台或声乐艺术。

entries.definition: Relating to opera, or exaggerated in the manner of opera.
entries.definitionCN: 与歌剧有关的，或像歌剧那样夸张的。

entries.definition: A work of art, especially a musical composition.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术作品，尤指音乐作品。

entries.definition: A short, light opera with spoken dialogue and songs.
entries.definitionCN: 有对白与唱段的短小轻歌剧。

entries.definition: A comic opera in the Italian tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利传统中的喜歌剧。

entries.definition: A stage show that mixes songs, dance and spoken scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 把歌曲、舞蹈与对白场面混合的舞台演出。

entries.definition: A long musical work on a sacred subject, sung without staging.
entries.definitionCN: 以宗教题材写成、只唱不演的长篇音乐作品。

entries.definition: A staged dance work with music but without singing.
entries.definitionCN: 有音乐、无歌唱的舞台舞蹈作品。

normalIntro.en: Opera is a Latin plural that Italian turned into the name of a sung play, and the family keeps circling the idea of a work.
normalIntro.cn: opera 本是拉丁语的复数形式，意大利语把它变成一路唱着演的戏剧之名；这一族词都绕着「作品」打转。

normal.en: Opera is the plural of opus, so the word literally means works.
normal.cn: opera 是 opus 的复数，字面上就是「多件作品」。

normal.en: The Latin phrase opera in musica is the seed of the modern sense: a work set to music.
normal.cn: 拉丁短语 opera in musica 是现代词义的种子：谱上音乐的「作品」。

normal.en: Opera house names the building after the art, a common pattern for theatres.
normal.cn: opera house 用艺术之名来命名建筑，这是剧院常见的命名方式。

normal.en: Operatic adds -ic, meaning belonging to opera or behaving like someone on its stage.
normal.cn: operatic 加 -ic，意为属于歌剧的，或像站在歌剧舞台上那样夸张。

normal.en: Operetta is a small opera, because the Italian diminutive makes the genre light and short.
normal.cn: operetta 是「小歌剧」，意大利语的指小形式让这个门类变得轻巧短小。

abstract.en: One word for works, a genre and a building shows how a single name can shelter a whole art.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指作品、门类和建筑，说明一个名字可以把一门艺术整个罩住。

abstract.en: The audience sits in the dark while a story is carried entirely by the human voice.
abstract.cn: 观众坐进黑暗里，整个故事只靠人声扛着走。

abstract.en: Singing turns ordinary speech into something too large for a living room.
abstract.cn: 歌唱把日常说话放大成客厅装不下的东西。

examples.en: The new opera was written by a young composer.
examples.cn: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。

examples.en: She has spent thirty years in opera.
examples.cn: 她在歌剧这一行干了三十年。

examples.en: The opera is rebuilding its stage this winter.
examples.cn: 歌剧院今年冬天要重修它的舞台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，泼啦」——台上唱得太投入，茶水泼了满地也不管；记住 opera 是歌剧。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果，属格 operis）的复数 opera 意为「作品」，意大利语用它指「谱成音乐的戏剧」，十七世纪传入英语。它与 operate 不是同一个词：operate 来自拉丁动词 operari（干活、起作用），两条路线不同，现代英语里不能互换。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a work set to music; the senses divide into one staged work, the art form as a whole, and the house or company that presents it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「谱成音乐的成品」；义项分为一部具体的舞台作品、作为整体的艺术门类，以及上演它的场所或团体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a singer standing before a painted set while the orchestra waits in the pit.
core.cn: 核心意象：歌唱者站在彩绘布景前，乐队在乐池里等最后一个音符。

branches.en: a young composer finishing a score late at night
branches.cn: 年轻作曲家深夜写完一部总谱

branches.en: the curtain falling after the last aria
branches.cn: 最后一段咏叹调唱完，幕布落下

branches.en: a singer choosing a life on the stage
branches.cn: 歌唱者选择以舞台为业

branches.en: a stone theatre lit up on opening night
branches.cn: 首演之夜灯火通明的石砌剧院

branches.en: a company loading scenery onto a truck for a tour
branches.cn: 剧团把布景装上卡车去巡演

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin plural for works, passes through Italian, and gathers English compounds for the house, the singer and the company.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「作品」的复数形式上，经意大利语中转，再在英语里聚起一批指剧院、演员和剧团的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind opera is the opus family: a work, its plural, and the adjectives built on them.
latinIntro.cn: opera 背后的拉丁词族是 opus 一族：作品、它的复数，以及由它们构成的形容词。

items.meaning: plural marker of the first declension

definition_zh: 操作；运转；经营；动手术
definition_en: to work or function, to control a machine, to run a business, or to perform a medical operation
core_image: 一只手按下按钮，整排机器依次发出低响，像身体里某处重新开始供血
scene: 深夜的泵房里，值班员按下启动键，旧水泵先抖了两下，随后平稳地响了起来。The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
sceneCN: 这里是「运转」（第 1 个义项：机器或系统开始工作并保持运行）；句意为换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。图中可辨识物件：泵房管道、启动键、压力表。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语过去分词词干加 -tion 构成，义为「操作；手术；运算」
由拉丁语 operator（干活的人）进入英语，义为「操作员；运算符」
由 operari 加 -ive 构成，义为「起作用的；实施中的」

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to work or function, especially of a machine, system or service
senses.definitionCN: 尤指机器、系统或服务在工作、起作用
senses.example: The heating system operates at low cost in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这套供暖系统冬天运行成本很低。
senses.why: Latin operari means to work, so a machine that runs is the old idea of working moved from a person onto a device.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operari 意为「干活」，机器在运行这个义项，就是把「干活」从人身上挪到了装置上。

senses.title: To control a machine
senses.definition: to control or use a machine, vehicle or piece of equipment
senses.definitionCN: 控制并使用机器、车辆或设备
senses.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
senses.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。
senses.why: If a machine can work by itself, a person can also make it work, and the transitive use simply adds a hand on the controls.
senses.whyCN: 机器既然能自己运行，人也能使它运行；及物用法只是在「干活」这件事上多了一只放在操纵杆上的手。

senses.title: To perform surgery
senses.definition: to cut into a patient's body in order to treat a disease or an injury
senses.definitionCN: 切开病人身体以治疗疾病或损伤
senses.example: Surgeons operated on her knee at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在黎明时为她做了膝关节手术。
senses.why: Surgery is skilled work done with the hands on the body, so the general verb for working took the medical sense through the phrase operate on.
senses.whyCN: 手术是靠双手在身体上完成的技艺活，于是「干活」这个泛用动词借着 operate on 这个说法，担起了医学含义。

senses.title: To run a business or organization
senses.definition: to manage or run a business, service or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或经营一项生意、服务或组织
senses.example: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。
senses.why: Running an organization is continuous work, so the same verb moves from a single machine to a whole enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 经营一个组织是持续不断的活，同一个动词就这样从一台机器扩大到整个机构。

intro.en: Operate comes straight from Latin, where a verb for working gave English both the verb and its nouns; it is not the same word as opera, which arrived through Italian.
intro.cn: operate 直接从拉丁语进入英语，那里一个意为「干活」的动词为英语提供了动词和它的名词；它与经意大利语而来的 opera 不是同一个词。

items.en: Latin opus named work or a product, and its genitive operis supplied the stem for the verbs of working.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作或成果，属格 operis 为表示「干活」的一系列动词提供了词干。

items.en: Operari was a deponent verb meaning to work, to labor or to produce an effect.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为干活、劳作或产生作用。

items.en: Its past participle operatus meant having worked, and this is the form English took when it borrowed the verb.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 operatus 意为「已经干过」，英语借入动词时带的就是这个形式。

items.en: Early English operate meant to produce an effect or to exert force, a sense still heard in the word operation.
items.cn: 早期的英语 operate 意为产生效果或施加力量，这层意思至今还能在 operation 里听到。

items.en: Modern English widened operate to machines, businesses and surgery while keeping the older sense of having an effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把 operate 扩展到机器、企业和手术，同时保留了「起作用」这层旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin-derived working family; the near-meaning group is everyday verbs for running or handling something.
note.cn: 形近组是由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是日常里表示运转或摆弄某物的动词。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Working, or used for working, as in an operating system.
entries.definitionCN: 运转的或用于运转的，如操作系统。

entries.definition: A person who works a machine or handles telephone calls.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或处理电话的人。

entries.definition: Working or in force, and also a person who carries out secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，也指从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: To make a machine or a business work.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器或企业运转。

entries.definition: To work in the normal or expected way.
entries.definitionCN: 以正常或预期的方式工作。

entries.definition: To use or control something with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 用手使用或控制某物。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to the Latin verb for working, so the mnemonics follow the work from hands to machines to bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都可追到拉丁语表示「干活」的动词，所以联想沿着「活」从双手走到机器，再到身体。

normal.en: Operari means to work, so operate is first of all to be busy doing something.
normal.cn: operari 意为干活，所以 operate 首先是「在忙着做某事」。

normal.en: Operation adds -tion and turns the working into a thing you can name.
normal.cn: operation 加 -tion，把「干活」变成一个可以叫出名字的东西。

normal.en: Operator adds -or and turns the working into the person who does it.
normal.cn: operator 加 -or，把「干活」变成干活的那个人。

normal.en: Operate on is the medical phrase, where the body is the thing being worked on.
normal.cn: operate on 是医学说法，被「干活」的对象就是身体。

normal.en: Operative means still at work, which is why a spy is also called one.
normal.cn: operative 意为仍在起作用，这就是特工也被叫作 operative 的原因。

abstract.en: A hand on a lever is the shortest picture of operate: effort passing into a machine.
abstract.cn: 一只手搭在操纵杆上，就是 operate 最短的画面：力气传进机器。

abstract.en: A machine that runs is a person's work continuing after the person has stepped away.
abstract.cn: 机器自己转着，就是人的活在离开之后还继续着。

abstract.en: Cutting a body to mend it shows how far the plain word for working can travel.
abstract.cn: 切开身体去修补它，说明「干活」这个平常词能走多远。

examples.en: The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
examples.cn: 换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。

examples.en: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
examples.cn: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。

examples.en: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，怕累他」——机器开动以后，最怕累坏那个守着它的人；记住 operate 是操作、运转。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果）派生动词 operari（干活、起作用），过去分词 operatus 进入英语成为 operate；同族词有 operation、operator、operative、operating。opera 虽与它共享更远的拉丁词根，却经意大利语而来、指「歌剧」，不能与 operate 混用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is work being done; the senses move from a machine running, to a hand controlling it, to surgery, and finally to running a whole enterprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「正在干的活」；义项从机器自己运行，移到人伸手操纵，再到在身体上动刀，最后到经营整个机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a button and a row of machines answering with a low hum.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下按钮，一排机器用低沉的声音回应。

branches.en: a pump finding its rhythm after a repair
branches.cn: 修好之后水泵重新找到节奏

branches.en: an operator guiding a crane over a roof
branches.cn: 操作员把起重机吊过屋顶

branches.en: a trainee learning to keep both hands still
branches.cn: 学徒练习让两只手保持不动

branches.en: a lamp above a table in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里，台面上方的一盏灯

branches.en: a small office counting the shelters it runs
branches.cn: 小办公室清点自己经营的那几家收容所

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned English verb, and the family adds -tion for the act, -or for the person and -ive for the working quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词变成的英语动词；同族词用 -tion 表示行为，用 -or 表示人，用 -ive 表示「起作用的」性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind operate is the working branch of the opus family: the verb, its participle and the agent noun.
latinIntro.cn: operate 背后的拉丁语是 opus 一族里「干活」的那一支：动词、分词和施事名词。

definition_en: the working of a machine or system, a planned activity, a surgical treatment, or a mathematical process
core_image: 手术灯下，主刀医生的手停在心脏上方，旁边屏幕上跳动着体外循环机的运行曲线
scene: 手术灯亮起后，主刀医生用两个小时完成了孩子心脏上的一处修补。The hospital performed a delicate operation on the child's heart that morning.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「在身体上施行的外科手术」（第 3 个义项：由医生切开或进入体内完成的治疗）；句意为那天上午医院为孩子的心脏做了一台精细手术。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、体外循环机、监护屏、无菌手套；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The working of a machine or system
senses.definition: the way in which a device, plant or system performs its function
senses.definitionCN: 装置、工厂或系统发挥功能的方式
senses.example: The pump's operation is monitored from a control room.
senses.exampleCN: 泵的运转由控制室监控。
senses.why: The word rests on a Latin verb meaning to work, so the working of a system is its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「工作」动词之上，因此系统的运转是它最字面的义项。

senses.title: The act of making a device work
senses.definition: the act of running or controlling a machine by hand or by control
senses.definitionCN: 用手或控制装置使机器运行的动作
senses.example: Operation of the crane requires two trained hands.
senses.exampleCN: 操作这台吊车需要两名受过训练的人。
senses.why: Doing the work and making something else work are two sides of one verb, so the act of driving a machine took the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自己干活与让别的东西干活是同一个动词的两面，因此驱动机器的动作也用了这个名词。

senses.title: A surgical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment in which a surgeon cuts into or enters the body to repair it
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生切开或进入体内进行修补的治疗
senses.example: The operation on her knee lasted two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖的手术持续了两个小时。
senses.why: Surgery is work done on a body, so medicine used the general noun for work and it became the everyday word for an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 手术是对身体所做的工作，因此医学用这个泛指「工作」的名词，它后来成了介入治疗的日常说法。

senses.title: A planned military action
senses.definition: an organized movement of forces with a set aim, usually given a name
senses.definitionCN: 有明确目标、通常有代号的部队组织行动
senses.example: The rescue operation began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在黎明开始。
senses.why: Military staffs speak of work done by combined forces as one operation, and the sense spread to any coordinated action.
senses.whyCN: 军事参谋把多支部队合力完成的工作称为一次行动，这个义项后来扩展到任何协同行动。

senses.title: The everyday activities of a business
senses.definition: the routine activities by which a company or institution keeps running, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构维持运转的日常活动，常用复数
senses.example: The firm moved its operations closer to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把业务迁到离港口更近的地方。
senses.why: A business is a set of workings, so its routine activities are called its operations rather than its plans.
senses.whyCN: 一家企业就是一组运转，因此它的日常活动被称为业务，而不是计划。

senses.title: A mathematical process
senses.definition: a rule applied to numbers or symbols to produce a new value
senses.definitionCN: 施于数字或符号以得出新值的规则
senses.example: Addition is the first operation children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 加法是孩子学的第一种运算。
senses.why: Mathematics treats each rule as work performed on symbols, which is the same idea of a working applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 数学把每条规则看作对符号所做的工作，这与「运转」是同一个意思，只是对象换成数字。

senses.title: A running business or unit
senses.definition: an enterprise or a distinct unit that is being run as a going concern
senses.definitionCN: 作为持续经营体运作的企业或独立单位
senses.example: The mine is a profitable operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿是一个盈利的经营单位。
senses.why: Once a business is seen as something that works, the thing that works can itself be called an operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业被看作在运转的东西，这个在运转的东西本身就可以被称为一个经营单位。

senses.title: An organized piece of work with a plan
senses.titleCN: 有组织的行动；专项行动
senses.definition: a coordinated piece of work, often large, carried out by a group toward one aim
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人朝同一目标实施的、常具规模的协同工作
senses.example: The cleanup operation involved three hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次清理行动动用了三百名志愿者。
senses.why: Any large piece of coordinated work can be called an operation, because it is work organized as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何大规模协同工作都可称为一次行动，因为它被组织成一个整体的运作。

intro.en: Operation came through Old French from Latin operatio 'a working', built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. The origin of opus before Latin is unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「工作」的名词，其基础为表示「工作」的动词与名词。名词词根在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work, a task'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品、任务」。其在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，有时为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Operari, a deponent verb, meant 'to work, to labour, to perform'.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为「工作、劳作、施行」。

items.en: Operatio, from operari plus the noun suffix -io, named a working or the result of working.
items.cn: operatio 由 operari 加名词后缀 -io 构成，指工作这一动作或其结果。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first for any action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指任何动作或效果。

items.en: From the seventeenth century surgery adopted the word for an intervention, and from the eighteenth military staffs used it for a named action.
items.cn: 十七世纪起外科把这个词用于介入治疗，十八世纪起军事参谋用它指有代号的行动。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin noun of work, plus one that only looks similar; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「工作」名词的词，外加一个仅形似的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: To run a machine, to carry on business or to perform surgery; the noun names the working, the verb performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指运转机器、开展业务或施行手术；名词指运转本身，动词指施行。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine or a business, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指操作机器或经营业务的人。

entries.definition: Co- 'together' plus the same verb: joint work, with no single unit of action.
entries.definitionCN: co-「共同」加同一动词：指共同工作，不指单个动作单元。

entries.definition: From orare 'to speak', not from opus: a formal speech, similar only in its ending.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 orare「说话」，而非 opus：指正式演说，仅词尾相似。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine and the procedure itself, with nothing about machines or business.
entries.definitionCN: 指外科这一学科及手术本身，与机器或业务无关。

entries.definition: The ordered steps of an action; it does not imply that anything is actually running.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的有序步骤，并不表示事情真的在运转。

entries.definition: The proper role or capacity of a part; it names what something is for, not how it runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指某部件的应有作用或能力，说明它用于什么，而非如何运转。

entries.definition: A connected series of actions for one aim, often public or military; it stresses duration, not a single working.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标展开的系列行动，常为宣传或军事行动；强调持续时间，而非单次运作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Latin noun of work plus a noun suffix: the doing of work, and then any piece of work that is done.
normal.cn: 拉丁「工作」名词加名词后缀：先指干活，再指所干的任一件事。

normal.en: One root yields the verb to run, the person who runs, the adjective for running order and the noun for joint work.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出表示运转的动词、表示操作者的名词、表示运转状态的形容词，以及表示合作的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: in operation, surgical operation, rescue operation, daily operations.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：在运转中、外科手术、救援行动、日常业务。

normal.en: Hospitals, armies and mathematics all call their own kind of work by this one name.
normal.cn: 医院、军队与数学都把自己那类工作用同一个名称来称呼。

normal.en: A factory is said to be in operation, and later the factory itself is called an operation.
normal.cn: 工厂被说成处于运转中，后来工厂本身也被称为一个经营单位。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose gears keep turning while nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的齿轮在无人注视时仍不停转动。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon's hands as the only still thing in a room full of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子机器都在动，只有外科医生的手是静的。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that changes when one rule is applied.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字在施加一条规则后整体改变。

examples.en: The plant has been in operation since the river was dammed.
examples.cn: 这座工厂自河流筑坝以来一直在运转。

examples.en: The peacekeeping operation was extended for another six months.
examples.cn: 维和行动又延长了六个月。

examples.en: Division is the operation most often done wrong under time pressure.
examples.cn: 除法是时间紧迫时最容易算错的一种运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oper（工作）+ ation（名词）」——在工作、在运转 → 运转、操作、手术、行动、运算

root: 拉丁语「工作」名词派生出「工作、施行」的动词，再加后缀构成「工作、运作」的名词；名词词根更早的来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of working: a machine runs, a hand makes it run, a surgeon works on a body, an army works on an objective, a company works every day, a rule works on numbers, a working enterprise is itself a unit, and any coordinated effort is one operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「工作」动作展开：机器运转、手使它运转、医生在身体上工作、军队对一个目标行动、公司每天运作、规则对数字起作用、运转中的企业本身成为一个单位，最后任何协同用力都算一次行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gears turning under a lamp while a hand rests on the switch that keeps them turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下齿轮转动，一只手按在使它们继续转动的开关上。

branches.en: RUNNING AND DRIVING: the working of a system and the act that keeps it working are one event seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 运转与驱动：系统的运转与使它运转的动作，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: ON A BODY: surgery is work performed on flesh with tools.
branches.cn: 施于身体：手术是用工具在血肉上所做的工作。

branches.en: ON AN AIM: a named military action and any coordinated effort are work organized toward one end.
branches.cn: 对准目标：有代号的军事行动与任何协同工作，都是朝一个目标组织起来的劳动。

branches.en: THE WORKING UNIT: a company's daily business and the enterprise itself are the same working seen as activity and as thing.
branches.cn: 运转单位：公司的日常业务与企业本身，是同一个运转被看作活动与看作实体。

branches.en: ON SYMBOLS: arithmetic applies the same notion of work to numbers.
branches.cn: 施于符号：算术把同一个「工作」观念用在数字上。

intro.en: Operation is a Latin noun of work: a root noun for a task and a verb for doing it, with a suffix that turns the doing into a name.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「工作」的拉丁名词：一个指任务的词根名词、一个指做这件事的动词，以及把「做」变成名称的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus and operari give operate, operator, operation and cooperation; the noun suffix marks the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「工作」的名词与动词衍生出运转、操作者与合作等词；名词后缀标记动作或其结果。

items.example: The root noun names the task itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词指任务本身。

items.example: The verb turns the task into activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把任务变成活动。

items.example: The suffix makes the activity a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把活动变成可计数的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the activity and its result.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指动作与其结果。

items.example: The suffix is the same one that builds many nouns of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成许多表示过程的名词。

items.example: One verb covers machines, businesses and surgeons.
items.exampleCN: 一个动词兼指机器、企业与外科医生。

items.meaning: one who works a machine or business
items.meaningCN: 操作机器或经营业务的人
items.example: The agent suffix names the person at the controls.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指在控制台前的人。

items.example: The prefix makes the work shared.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使这份工作成为共享的。

items.meaningCN: 处于运转状态的；生效的
items.example: A rule becomes operative when it starts to apply.
items.exampleCN: 规则开始适用时便生效。
